E01.title: Change one spring: which cells of K change?
E01.lead: Three springs in a chain, a wall on the left, 60 N pulling on the right. Every finite element program ends up solving K u = f. Here you build that K yourself, one spring at a time.

E02.title: The weak form: why we rewrite the heat equation
E02.lead: An aluminum bar, 4 cm long, makes 80 W of heat along its length; both ends are held at 20 °C. A broken line of two straight pieces can't go into its equation. Rewrite the equation, and it can. Here you find the middle temperature yourself, by balancing one hat.

E03.title: Exact at the nodes? Finite elements in Python
E03.lead: The same heated bar as episode 2 (4 cm, 80 W, both ends at 20 °C), now cut into 4 and then 8 elements and solved by a short program. Guess a node, then cut the bar finer yourself and watch where the error hides.

E04.title: More nodes, worse answer? Shape functions
E04.lead: The same 4 cm bar, but now all 80 W comes from a heater 0.4 cm wide in the middle. Take the exact temperatures at 11 nodes and join them two ways: 10 straight pieces, or one smooth curve of degree 10. Guess which is closer, then try more nodes yourself.
